quote: Anyway, you know, we had spoke to somebody a long time ago about it.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior solar conversation; rep never asks which company or what happened.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be deliberately not dwelling on a negative story to keep momentum — but nothing later shows this paid off; the grievance resurfaces worse at 04:05.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what company was that, and what happened?' — surfaces competitive context and defuses the trust wound before it compounds.

quote: they never did wind up never showing up.
stewart_read: Customer names being stood up by a competitor; rep responds with a flat 'Okay' and changes subject to state/address.
coaching_implication: A one-line acknowledgment ('that's frustrating, we'll make sure that doesn't happen here') would directly counter the customer's live fear.

quote: She said we never received an appointment from the other outfit after we sent all our electric... paperwork
stewart_read: Third mention of the same ghosting grievance, now with more detail (paperwork sent, no appointment came); rep pivots immediately to a meter-location qualifier.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a deliberate refusal to relitigate a competitor's failure — but the customer is signaling exactly what he needs reassurance on before trusting this process again.
coaching_implication: This is the moment to promise concretely that Ion will follow through, tying it to the appointment commitment about to be made.

quote: And then do you know how much you spend on a monthly average?
stewart_read: Bill amount deflected to spouse; rep never attempts to get even a ballpark or loop the wife in, and never returns to it after moving to the kWh-graph text ask.
coaching_implication: Should have asked 'any idea, even roughly?' or flagged the wife needs to be on the eventual appointment since she owns the bill knowledge.

quote: So what does it cost me out of pocket to get it?
stewart_read: Rep answers the no-upfront-cost mechanic reasonably, but never flips it back to the customer's own bill as the real expense he should fear.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep's answer is schema-compliant on the mechanism (bill swap) even if it doesn't use the sharper inversion language — a partial credit, not a full miss.
coaching_implication: Land the flip explicitly: 'what's costing you is the bill you're paying now — this just lowers it with nothing out of pocket.'

quote: And I I was just starting to look at that ad, and then I got a phone call, so I you know? And then you called.
stewart_read: Customer confirms he was actively engaging with the solar ad moments before the call — strong self-initiated interest signal.
coaching_implication: Rep could reflect this back ('you were already digging into it — let's get you real numbers') to build momentum instead of moving straight to logistics.
